overview: The Medford Historical Commission found 141 Grant Avenue preferably preserved under the demolition delay ordinance, determined 33 Winchester Street and 387–389 Main Street to be historically significant, and advised the Islamic Cultural Center of Medford on potential alterations to the Isaac Hall House. The commission also adopted its 2027 meeting calendar, reviewed ongoing local preservation projects, and recognized outgoing chair Jennifer Keenan for her service.

items.title: 141 Grant Avenue Public Hearing
items.summary: The commission voted to determine the property preferably preserved, enacting an 18-month demolition delay while the applicant collaborates with a subcommittee on design modifications.

items.title: 33 Winchester Street Demolition Review
items.summary: After accepting the demolition delay application, the commission voted that the structure is historically significant and scheduled a public hearing for December.

items.title: 387–389 Main Street Demolition Review
items.summary: The commission determined the commercial and residential property historically significant, referring the proposed alterations to a public hearing next month.

items.title: Isaac Hall House Project Update
items.summary: Humayun Morshed sought guidance on adapting 43 High Street for expanded prayer and community space, and commissioners recommended retaining a preservation architect and exploring future Community Preservation Act funding.

items.title: 2027 Meeting Schedule and Board Officers
items.summary: Approved the 2027 meeting dates calendar and discussed upcoming committee roles and officer vacancies ahead of annual leadership transitions.

items.title: Project Updates, Minutes, and Recognition of Jennifer Keenan
items.summary: Commissioners discussed demolition inquiries for 33 Capen Street, zoning updates, Medford High School historical documentation, approved the October 19 minutes, and commended former chair Jennifer Keenan for nine years of service.
